subject: Annualized billing swap — phased ramp, step discounts, and payment cadence
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme.ai>; Tom Weaver <t.weaver@acme.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Annualized billing swap — phased ramp, step discounts, and payment cadence

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the deep dive this week. As discussed, we've sketched an approach to move Acme from monthly/quarterly pay-as-you-go to an annualized committed contract with a staged ramp to protect you from over-commitment in early months while giving you predictable unit economics. The attached proposal lays out three core elements:

1) Term and discounting: 12‑month commitment with a tiered discount schedule (0–6m: 10% off hosted unit price, 7–12m: 18% off). The idea is to reward growth while keeping early risk lower.
2) Phased ramp: monthly true-up checkpoints with a one-time catch-up credit if actual usage exceeds the committed baseline by >20% in months 1–3. After month 4 we shift to the contracted ramp cadence.
3) Payment and accounting: annual invoicing up-front preferred; alternatively, we can sign a 12‑month commitment with quarterly invoicing + irrevocable payment terms. We included an option with a 2% finance fee if you require quarterly invoicing.

Open questions for procurement/finance on your side: preferred invoice cadence, whether Acme needs PO/ERP specific wording, and whether a performance clause is required for SLA credits.

Attachment: Redwood_Annual_Swap_Proposal_ACME_v1.pdf (proposal summary)

Next steps: if this structure looks reasonable, I can route a SOW + pricing workbook for your finance team and loop legal for a light redline. Can we aim for an internal procurement review by Oct 22?

Best,
Priyom
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0192

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Weaver <t.weaver@acme.ai>, finance@acme.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Annualized billing swap — phased ramp, step discounts, and payment cadence

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the PDF. A few quick items from finance:

- They prefer annual invoicing if there's a material discount (good).
- Any ability to move more of the discount earlier? First 3 months are where our pilot runs and we want lower unit cost to validate features without being cash-heavy.
- We need a clause for usage true-ups to be capped per quarter. No open-ended back bills across the year.

Also, please send the pricing workbook so our FP&A can run the numbers. Procurement asked for sample payment terms and whether Redwood can accept our standard PO language (we'll attach their template).

Could you also confirm timing for onboarding milestones so we can map budget recognition?

Samantha
Head of Product Operations, Acme AI
Samantha.Ortiz@acme.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, finance@acme.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Annualized billing swap — phased ramp, step discounts, and payment cadence

Samantha —

Appreciate the specifics. Quick replies inline:

- Early discount: we can shift a portion of the step discount forward: option A gives 14% discount months 0–3, then 16% months 4–12 (net ARR similar, but front-loads savings). Option B is the previously sent 10% then 18% split. I'll attach an updated pricing-model-acme-annual.xlsx with both scenarios.
- True-up cap: agree to a quarterly true-up cap of 25% (i.e., we won't invoice more than +25% of committed baseline for any quarter without prior notice). Any overage beyond that will be subject to negotiation and documented in the SOW.
- Payment terms: annual prepay preferred; if you need quarterly billing, we can accept but add a 2% fee or shorten net terms to Net30. We can accept your PO language with two minor clauses added: (1) a short SLA credit process, (2) confidentiality/data handling confirmation to satisfy our auditors.

Onboarding milestones: we propose milestone A (pilot kick-off) within 2 weeks of signature, milestone B (production roll) within 8 weeks, milestone C (Q1 operational review) at month 3. We can map these to deferred revenue recognition buckets for you — will include in the SOW.

Attachments: pricing-model-acme-annual.xlsx, ACME_SOW-draft.docx

If this aligns, I can ask Legal to accept your PO template and prepare a DocuSign for review. What's your target signature date?

Best,
Priyom
From: Tom Weaver <t.weaver@acme.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Annualized billing swap — phased ramp, step discounts, and payment cadence

On Mon, Oct 19, 2026 at 08:47 AM Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com> wrote:
> Priyom
>
> Appreciate the specifics. Quick replies inline:

Thanks — the quarterly true-up cap and the front-loaded discount option A look reasonable. Two procurement asks: 1) our finance team wants a 60‑day payment window for the first invoice only (we can do Net30 thereafter), and 2) please confirm there will be no retroactive commitments applied to invoices after a signed period (i.e., agreed baseline stands unless both parties sign an amendment).

If Redwood is okay with those, I can push for internal sign-off this week. Also, can you confirm whether Redwood will provide usage reports at account-level weekly for the first two months (helps our ops team validate consumption against the committed baseline)?

Tom
VP Engineering, Acme AI
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme.ai>; Tom Weaver <t.weaver@acme.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Annualized billing swap — phased ramp, step discounts, and payment cadence

Tom / Samantha —

Short answers: yes.

- 60‑day first invoice window: acceptable as a one-off exception; subsequent invoices Net30. We'll add a clause to the SOW noting the one-time extended payment term.
- No retroactive commitments: agreed — the committed baseline is fixed at signature; changes require an amendment.
- Weekly usage reports: yes, we'll provide account-level usage reports every Monday for the first 8 weeks, then bi-weekly thereafter unless you prefer weekly longer. We'll include a report template with the SOW.

I'll loop legal to start a redline for the SOW and invoice term clause, then prepare a DocuSign envelope that captures the option A pricing (front-loaded 14%/16% split). If procurement confirms by end of day Thu Oct 22, we can target signature Oct 27 and kickoff the pilot the week of Nov 1.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Acme into production.

Priyom
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: Redwood_Annual_Swap_Proposal_ACME_v1.pdf, pricing-model-acme-annual.xlsx, ACME_SOW-draft.docx
